# GripPose

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Runtime/Scripts/Interaction/GripPose.cs#L27)

One authored hand shape at one [`GripPoint`](/api/vrframework-interaction-runtime/GripPoint): where the hand sits relative to the point,
and what its fingers do once it is there.

Data on the point rather than a hand parented under it. A hand under the object inherits the
object's scale, and a hand has one size - shrink the object and the grip that was authored on
it becomes a grip by a doll. It also put a skinned mesh into every scene that used one, and
left the author's working copy shipped inside the build.

What is stored is the *wrist*, in the point's own space, and not the place the hold
aligns to. Where a hand grips relative to its wrist belongs to the hand and differs between one
rig and the next, so each hand supplies its own when the object is picked up. Storing the grip
instead would bake one hand's build into every object authored while it was the hand.

The point's space rather than the object's, which is what makes a grip point that moves at run
time work: a lever's grip travels with the lever, and the hand on it travels with the grip
without anything having to be recomputed against the object.
